title: Statement of Cash Flows - Preparation and Classification
learning_objectives: Prepare statement of cash flows using indirect and direct methods
Classify cash flows into operating, investing, and financing activities
Reconcile net income to cash from operations

common_question_types: Prepare cash flow statement (indirect method most common)
Reconcile net income to operating cash flow
Calculate cash from operations or investing

overview.purpose: Report cash receipts and cash payments during a period, classified by operating, investing, and financing activities
overview.required_for: All entities that provide balance sheet and income statement
format_options: Indirect method (most common) - starts with net income
Direct method - shows gross cash receipts and payments

operating_activities.definition: Principal revenue-producing activities and other activities not classified as investing or financing
examples_outflows: Cash paid to suppliers and employees
operating_activities.indirect_method: Start with net income, adjust for noncash items and changes in working capital

investing_activities.definition: Acquisition and disposition of long-term assets and investments not included in cash equivalents

financing_activities.definition: Activities resulting in changes in size and composition of equity capital and borrowings

indirect_method.title: Indirect Method (Reconciliation Method)
operating_section_format: + Amortization of bond discount (or - amortization of premium)
+ Loss on sale of assets (or - gain on sale)

logic.add_back_noncash_expenses: Depreciation, amortization reduce NI but don't use cash
logic.gains_losses_on_investing_financing: Add back losses (or subtract gains) because actual cash flow in investing/financing sections

working_capital_changes.current_assets: Increase = use of cash (subtract). Decrease = source of cash (add).
working_capital_changes.current_liabilities: Increase = source of cash (add). Decrease = use of cash (subtract).

adjustments: + Decrease in accounts receivable: $10,000 (collected more than sales)
- Increase in inventory: $(15,000) (bought more than sold)
+ Increase in accounts payable: $8,000 (paid less than purchases)

direct_method.title: Direct Method
direct_method.rarely_used: Less than 1% of companies, but FASB prefers it
direct_method.reconciliation_required: If direct method used, must also provide reconciliation of net income to cash from operations (essentially showing indirect method)

calculations.cash_from_customers: Sales + Beginning AR - Ending AR (or Sales - Increase in AR)
calculations.cash_to_suppliers: COGS + Increase in Inventory + Decrease in AP (or COGS adjusted for inventory and AP changes)
calculations.cash_for_operating_expenses: Operating expenses - Depreciation + Decrease in Prepaid + Decrease in Accrued Liabilities (adjust for noncash and accrual changes)

classification_rules.interest_paid: Operating (controversial - some argue financing, but GAAP requires operating)
classification_rules.income_taxes_paid: Operating (unless directly related to investing/financing transaction)
classification_rules.payment_of_lease_principal: Financing (operating lease payments classified as operating)

gain_loss_on_sale_of_assets.income_statement: Gain or loss reported in net income

cash_flow_statement.operating_section: Add back loss or subtract gain (indirect method)
cash_flow_statement.investing_section: Report full cash proceeds from sale
cash_flow_statement.rationale: Remove from operating (noncash effect on NI), capture actual cash in investing

gain_loss_on_sale_of_assets.example: Equipment with book value $80K sold for $100K. Gain $20K. Operating section: Subtract $20K gain from NI. Investing section: Cash from sale of equipment $100K.

noncash_investing_financing.definition: Significant transactions that don't affect cash
examples: Acquisition of assets by issuing stock or debt
noncash_investing_financing.disclosure: NOT reported in statement body. Disclosed in supplemental schedule or notes.
noncash_investing_financing.example: Issued $500K of common stock to acquire land. Supplemental disclosure: 'Acquired land valued at $500K by issuing common stock.'

stock_dividends_and_splits.treatment: Noncash transaction - no effect on cash flow statement

operating_lease_accounting.asc_842: Lease payments classified as operating cash outflows

t_account_approach.description: Systematic method to prepare cash flow statement by reconstructing transactions
process: 1. Create T-accounts for each balance sheet account
2. Enter beginning and ending balances from comparative balance sheets
3. Reconstruct transactions that explain changes in account balances
4. Classify each transaction as operating, investing, or financing cash flow (or noncash)
5. Summarize to prepare statement of cash flows
t_account_approach.example_entry: If AR decreased $10K, reconstructed entry: DR Cash $10K, CR Accounts Receivable $10K. This is operating cash inflow (indirect method: Add to NI).

always_add_back: Deferred tax expense (increase in deferred tax liability)
always_subtract: Deferred tax benefit (decrease in deferred tax liability)

free_cash_flow.definition: Cash from operations - Capital expenditures - Dividends
free_cash_flow.alternative: Cash from operations - Capital expenditures (dividends optional in definition)
free_cash_flow.purpose: Measure of cash available for expansion, debt repayment, or distribution to shareholders
free_cash_flow.not_gaap: This is non-GAAP metric, not reported on statement of cash flows itself

comprehensive_example.scenario: Prepare operating section using indirect method

presentation: Net cash used in investing activities: $(67,000)
operating_adjustments: Gain on sale of equipment ($5K) subtracted from NI in operating section
Loss on sale of investments ($2K) added back to NI in operating section

presentation: Proceeds from issuance of common stock: $150,000
Net cash provided by financing activities: $235,000

reconciliation_to_balance_sheet.formula: Beginning Cash + Cash from Operations + Cash from Investing + Cash from Financing = Ending Cash
reconciliation_to_balance_sheet.note: Ending cash on cash flow statement must equal cash on balance sheet (verify accuracy)

cpa_exam_strategies.indirect_method: Start with NI. Add back noncash expenses (depreciation). Adjust for gains/losses on investing/financing. Adjust for working capital changes (assets opposite, liabilities same direction as cash).
cpa_exam_strategies.working_capital: Assets increase = subtract (use cash). Assets decrease = add (source cash). Liabilities increase = add (source cash). Liabilities decrease = subtract (use cash). Memory aid: ALDI (Assets ↓ = add, Liabilities ↑ = add).
cpa_exam_strategies.gain_loss: Add back losses, subtract gains (indirect method). Full proceeds in investing/financing sections.
cpa_exam_strategies.classification: Interest/dividends RECEIVED and interest PAID = operating. Dividends PAID = financing. PPE purchase/sale = investing.
cpa_exam_strategies.noncash: Significant noncash investing/financing transactions disclosed in supplemental schedule, NOT in statement body.
cpa_exam_strategies.most_tested: Preparing operating section (indirect method). Working capital adjustments. Classification of specific items.
cpa_exam_strategies.common_mistakes: Wrong direction for working capital changes. Forgetting to add back depreciation. Including noncash transactions in statement. Wrong classification of interest paid (it's operating).

key_points: Indirect method: Start with NI, adjust for noncash items and working capital changes
Direct method: Show gross cash receipts and payments (rarely used)
Adjust for gains/losses: Add losses, subtract gains (indirect method)
Working capital: Asset increases subtract, decreases add. Liability increases add, decreases subtract.
Interest and dividends received, interest paid = Operating. Dividends paid = Financing.
Noncash investing and financing disclosed supplementally, not in statement body
Ending cash must reconcile to balance sheet cash
